When concentration of B alone was doubled, the half-life did not change. When the concentration of A
alone was doubled, the rate increased by two times. The unit of rate constant for this reaction is
en.explanation:
Rate = k [A]x[B]y

When [B] is doubled, keeping [A] constant half-life of the reaction does not change.

For a first order reaction i.e. for a first order reaction does not depend up on the concentration. Hence the reaction is first order with respect to B. Now when [A] is doubled, keeping [B] constant, the rate also doubles. Hence the reaction is first order with respect to A.

Rate = k [A]1[B]1

Order of reaction
